openings.claim: Separate locating from gripping: each rod seats against two fixed adjacent faces and an end stop; an opposing adjustable plywood jaw presses it into those datums. Clearance elsewhere permits exchange without requiring a tight surrounding fit.
openings.delta: Change the positioning dependency from enclosing fit to fixed datum contacts and seat-before-clamp action. Cut the six plywood pieces into seat, stop and jaw parts; use the supplied bolts for fastening and adjustment, elastic loops for jaw return, and cord to retain every movable jaw, nut and washer. Drill plywood only; preserve the frame rod relationship within a measured 90 mm envelope.
openings.prediction: Nearest rival: tighter surrounding contact improves both restraint and return. The datum mechanism instead predicts that correctly seated clearance can return closer after exchange while resisting load. Distinguishing observations are target displacement before loading, displacement during loading, and exchange time; the supplied two trials establish neither explanation.
openings.probe: Use at most two configurations of the same captive hardware: generous clearance versus additional opposing-face contact, leaving datum positions unchanged. For each, log twelve exchanges: five per original rod, then two replacing the 19 mm rod with 18 mm. Apply four ten-second 10 N lateral load trials, including the replacement. Check the 2 mm circle and forty-second exchange limit. Stop fabrication at 100 minutes and testing at twenty minutes; report incomplete coverage explicitly.
assumptions: Existing rod alignment permits two seats inside 90 mm; supplied bolt lengths and cut-stock allocation permit captive fastening.
Hand tools can produce stable datum contacts and sufficient jaw stiffness; this is unmeasured.
Defeat: datum rocking, plywood bending, slip under load, or 18 mm travel exhaustion can invalidate the mechanism even with good unloaded return.

Reject any configuration needing rod modification, powered adjustment, loose exchange components, extra material, or more time. Repeated seating and loading must fit the twenty-minute capacity; a stop cap alone provides no evidence.
This is a fabrication and discrimination probe, not deployment or a promised pass.

assessment: One opening. It preserves the intended outcome and constraints but feasibility and load performance remain unknown. Configuration differences may also change preload, limiting causal attribution.
